blockers.title: The dependent-product predicate can erase the hostile cells that G16 must execute
blockers.counterexample: Take a component identity retained by the comparison-basis union and the required C-MISSING-COMPONENT-DECLARATION fixture. Delete or withhold that component declaration in the hostile input. coverageLaw includes a tuple only when 'that component's manifest declares the role and platform'; the declaration needed to admit the tuple is now absent, so the component x TypeScript x platform x C-MISSING-COMPONENT-DECLARATION cells fall outside the candidate's exact domain. Omitting them therefore is not an omitted in-domain cell and can satisfy the corpus without producing G16-3's required REFUSE result. The same escape exists for an absent/empty role or platform applicability declaration because no completeness rule or negative class retains those cells.
blockers.measurement: The domain has no immutable pre-mutation or comparison-basis definition and no non-shrink law. It also assigns role applicability to a component manifest, while the permitted governing bytes assign the slice-1 role list to D-002/DR-118 and assign per-component platform scope to the manifest. The only role references in the subject are the DR-118 dimension, this coverage predicate, G16-10, guidance, and repair prose; no authority, schema, digest, completeness, or refusal rule defines manifest-declared roles. 'Separately enumerated' deferred role/platform cells are required by prose but no such cell set is present in the contract.
blockers.risk: A harness can omit the very missing-declaration and missing-applicability negatives intended to prove fail-closed selection, yet appear complete under the self-shrinking exact-domain formula. That permits G16 qualification with an affected component untested, violating DR-G16's no-waiver rule and DR-121's change-impact/missed-dependency obligation.
blockers.suggestedFix: Define and digest a closed fixture-domain basis before hostile mutations: every comparison-basis component identity crossed with the product-selected DR-118 role set applicable to it, that component's validated nonempty platform set, and every change class. Hostile deletion/alteration MUST NOT shrink that basis. Missing/invalid role or platform metadata must retain the cell and force typed REFUSE/NON-PASS. Enumerate the D-002-deferred cells with owner/reason in an explicit closed set.

shouldFix.title: The four-value enum is present, but the policy and G16 oracle disagree on conflict-refuse
shouldFix.counterexample: A changed unit has two owners and the comparison-basis universe is independently complete. ambiguityPolicy lists REFUSE and SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE as options, and previewDefault says universe selection only when complete rather than making it mandatory. A conservative implementation emits a typed refusal with ambiguity=conflict-refuse. It conforms to the listed option and fail-safe law but fails G16-3, which says a complete C-MULTI-OWNER case 'is conflict-universe'.
shouldFix.measurement: The new enum correctly represents conflict-refuse. The surrounding law does not choose one complete-conflict resolution consistently. There is also no precedence for a multi-owner input whose universe is incomplete: step 3 and G16-3 describe incomplete universe as refuse-only while G16-3 separately calls C-MULTI-OWNER 'otherwise' conflict-refuse.
shouldFix.risk: Both resolutions are fail-safe, so this is not an under-selection blocker. It does make the selector contract and its acceptance oracle reject different implementations and prevents one deterministic typed interpretation of combined ambiguity conditions.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Choose and state MUST semantics for a complete conflict, then make G16-3 match. If both outcomes remain lawful, accept both conflict-refuse and conflict-universe for a complete conflict. Define precedence or orthogonal ambiguityClass/resolution fields for combined multi-owner plus incomplete-universe inputs.
